proof:
# Parity maxima: a residual certificate and a terminating volume forest

Let \(\mathcal C\subset\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, with \(n\ge1,d\ge2\), positive full mixed \(d\)-volume \(T\), and positive-fiber base set \(P\). Put \(N=2^n\). For every parity class \(c\), define
\[
 m_c=\max\{|K_z|:z\in P,\ z\equiv c\pmod2\},
 \qquad R=T-\sum_c m_c,                                  \tag{1}
\]
with \(m_c=0\) for a missing class. The maxima are attained because \(P\) is finite. The number \(R\) does not depend on how ties are resolved.

## 1. A necessary positive residual in every failing body

Let \(\rho_d>0\) be the dimension-only constant proved in candidate ff31d56304dd901a, and put
\[
                   c_d=\frac{\rho_d}{1+\rho_d}\in(0,1).  \tag{2}
\]
If no actual source point has depth at least \(\Gamma_d/N\), then
\[
             \boxed{\quad R>c_d\,\frac{T}{N}.\quad}      \tag{3}
\]

Indeed the own-fiber centroid bound implies \(|K_z|<T/N\) at every positive fiber; a fiber of mass \(T/N\) already suffices, including equality. Therefore every \(m_c<T/N\).

If a class is missing, \(\sum_c m_c<(N-1)T/N\), so \(R>T/N\), which is stronger than (3). More generally, if \(R<T/N\), all classes are present and
\[
 \min_c m_c
   =T-R-\sum_{c\ne c_{\min}}m_c
                   >\frac{T}{N}-R.                     \tag{4}
\]
If (3) failed, then \(R\le c_dT/N<T/N\). Choosing any attaining fiber in each class gives a complete positive parity core whose outside mass is exactly \(R\). Moreover
\[
 \frac{R}{\min_c m_c}
 \le \frac{R}{T/N-R}\le\rho_d,                           \tag{5}
\]
with a strict first inequality when \(R>0\); when \(R=0\) the ratio is zero directly. The parity-core theorem supplies the allegedly absent OC point, a contradiction.

Thus (3) is a quantified necessary residual condition, not an assertion that every source has a small residual. It uses the full-volume case \(q=d\). No varying-direction intrinsic extension of the core theorem is asserted here.

## 2. A terminating midpoint forest without an empty-hull hypothesis

The following separate result holds for \(d\ge1\), and does not require all parity classes to occur. In each occupied class choose a volume-maximizing base \(v_c\); among its volume maximizers, minimize \(|v_c|^2\), resolving any remaining ties arbitrarily. For \(z\in P\), define
\[
                     F(z)=\frac{z+v_{[z]}}2.             \tag{6}
\]
Convexity gives \(F(z)\in P\), since
\[
                \frac{K_z+K_{v_{[z]}}}2\subset K_{F(z)}. \tag{7}
\]
Let \(w_z=|K_z|>0\). Brunn--Minkowski implies
\[
 w_{F(z)}^{1/d}\ge
             \frac{w_z^{1/d}+m_{[z]}^{1/d}}2
                         \ge w_z^{1/d}.                 \tag{8}
\]
If \(w_z<m_{[z]}\), the volume increases strictly. If \(w_z=m_{[z]}\) but \(z\ne v_{[z]}\), the choice of the root gives
\[
 |F(z)|^2
 =\frac{|z|^2+|v_{[z]}|^2}{2}
                   -\frac{|z-v_{[z]}|^2}{4}
                         <|z|^2.                        \tag{9}
\]
Thus the lexicographic potential \((-w_z,|z|^2)\) strictly decreases at every nonroot: either the first coordinate decreases, or volumes remain equal and the second coordinate decreases. On the finite set \(P\), all orbits terminate. The fixed points are precisely the chosen parity maximizers.

Every target has at most \(N\) preimages, since a preimage from class \(c\) must equal \(2y-v_c\). There is no assumption that the roots form an empty lattice polytope, nor that they are in convex position. This differs from the geometric witness forest in candidate 668ad0ef7a63372e, whose termination used emptiness of the witness hull.

There is also an exact uniform mass-growth lower bound:
\[
 \boxed{\quad
       w_{F(z)}-w_z\ge2^{-d}(m_{[z]}-w_z).
       \quad}                                           \tag{10}
\]
To prove it put \(x=w_z^{1/d}\), \(y=m_{[z]}^{1/d}=x+t\), \(t\ge0\). The binomial formula, or monotonicity in the initial point, gives
\[
 (2x+t)^d-(2x)^d\ge(x+t)^d-x^d.
\]
Divide by \(2^d\) and use (8). The coefficient \(2^{-d}\) is sharp as \(w_z/m_{[z]}\to0\). The stronger root estimate (8) retains more information.

Repeated substitution also gives the actual Minkowski inclusion along every terminating path, exactly as in the archived forest. Its transported copies need not be disjoint. This new termination rule therefore does not by itself transfer cap depth or conserve the total source mass inside a root fiber.

## 3. Large residual does not force a uniform midpoint-growth gap

The following exact family has unique parity maxima, so this limitation cannot be blamed on ties. Fix a \(d\)-body \(K\) of volume one and \(0<\epsilon<1/3\), and set
\[
 \mathcal C_\epsilon
       =\{(z,x):0\le z\le3,\ x\in(1-\epsilon z)K\}.
                                                               \tag{11}
\]
This is a full-dimensional convex body: weighted Minkowski sums of positive homothetic copies of \(K\) give exactly the copy at the weighted average base. Its four actual integer fibers have roots and masses
\[
 f_i=1-i\epsilon,\qquad w_i=(1-i\epsilon)^d,\quad i=0,1,2,3.
\]
The unique even maximum is \(v_0=0\), and the unique odd maximum is \(v_1=1\). Hence
\[
 F(0)=0,\quad F(1)=1,\quad F(2)=1,\quad F(3)=2.
\]
For every edge the midpoint inclusion is equality, and the complete Brunn--Minkowski root slack is exactly zero:
\[
                    2f_{F(i)}-f_i-f_{v_{[i]}}=0.       \tag{12}
\]
Nevertheless
\[
 R=w_2+w_3,\qquad
 \frac RT\longrightarrow\frac12\quad(\epsilon\downarrow0).
                                                               \tag{13}
\]
Even the total unweighted volume increase on the two nonroot edges tends to zero:
\[
 \sum_{i=2,3}(w_{F(i)}-w_i)=w_1-w_3\longrightarrow0.
                                                               \tag{14}
\]
Thus no positive constant depending only on the dimensions can lower-bound either total BM root slack or the sum in (14) by a positive multiple of \(R\), even at fixed \(n=1,d\), with strict parity maxima and only four fibers.

For an exact rational instance, take \(\epsilon=1/q\), integer \(q\ge4\), and a rational simplex \(K\). Then
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i=2,3}(w_{F(i)}-w_i)}{R}
       =\frac{(q-1)^d-(q-3)^d}{(q-2)^d+(q-3)^d}
                                      \longrightarrow0. \tag{15}
\]
The affine-profile geometry makes (12) exact for every \(q\), not just in the limit.

The residual theorem and the forest are useful different constraints: failure must leave a quantified residual, and the volume-maximizer choice gives a finite descent. Their combination does not yet supply a cap charge. In particular the forest's available scalar growth can be arbitrarily small while its residual mass remains macroscopic. The existing cap-transport obstruction still prevents treating the overlapping arriving copies as disjoint mass.

The exact accounting and rational family are checked by ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_parity_residual_and_volume_forest.py; compactness in the parity-core theorem remains its separately proved dependency.
